microtheory.name: language_acquisition_linguistics
microtheory.definition: How children learn language. Critical period, poverty of the stimulus debate, statistical learning, Universal Grammar (Chomsky) vs usage-based (Tomasello), bootstrapping. Substrate analogue: substrate's own developmental loop applied to its linguistic capability.

concepts.name: language_acquisition_device
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1965. Innate cognitive module containing UG. Enables children to acquire any human language from limited input. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded language Mts as developmental scaffold.

concepts.name: poverty_of_stimulus
concepts.definition: Chomsky 1980. Children acquire grammar despite degenerate + impoverished input. Logical problem of language acquisition. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-prior need for sparse input.

concepts.name: universal_grammar_innate
concepts.definition: Specific linguistic knowledge present at birth. Principles + parameters. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational Mts present at seed.

concepts.name: parameter_setting
concepts.definition: Children set values of parametric switches (head-first vs head-last, pro-drop, etc.) from input. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-instance parameter-fitting from experience.

concepts.name: statistical_learning
concepts.definition: Saffran 1996. Infants extract patterns from input by tracking transitional probabilities. Substrate analogue: substrate's distributional pattern detection.

concepts.name: usage_based_acquisition
concepts.definition: Tomasello. Grammar emerges from cognitive + social processes operating on usage. No innate UG needed. Substrate analogue: substrate's bottom-up Mt formation.

concepts.name: constructions_in_acquisition
concepts.definition: Children acquire item-based constructions before generalizing. 'Daddy go', 'Mommy go'. Substrate analogue: substrate's instance-to-pattern generalization.

concepts.name: frequency_in_acquisition
concepts.definition: High-frequency forms acquired earlier. Type vs token frequency. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-biased learning.

concepts.name: milestones_acquisition
concepts.definition: Cooing (3mo), babbling (6mo), first words (12mo), 2-word combinations (18mo), vocabulary explosion (18-24mo), complex sentences (3yr). Universal sequence. Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental phase transitions.

concepts.name: critical_period_language
concepts.definition: Window for full language acquisition, ending ~puberty. Genie, Wild Boy of Aveyron, deaf children of hearing parents. Substrate analogue: substrate's plasticity-override window.

concepts.name: vocabulary_explosion_acquisition
concepts.definition: 18-24mo. Acquisition rate jumps from ~1/week to ~10/day. Quine's gavagai problem solved by joint attention + mutual exclusivity. Substrate analogue: substrate's phase-transition in lexical acquisition.

concepts.name: overregularization
concepts.definition: Children produce 'goed', 'mouses' — U-shaped curve: correct → wrong → correct. Shows rule extraction. Substrate analogue: substrate's rule-application across exceptions.

concepts.name: mutual_exclusivity
concepts.definition: Markman 1989. Children assume each object has one label. Constraint biasing word learning. Substrate analogue: substrate's anti-redundancy bias in Concept formation.

concepts.name: whole_object_constraint
concepts.definition: New label refers to whole object, not part. Substrate analogue: substrate's gestalt-biased Concept formation.

concepts.name: taxonomic_constraint
concepts.definition: New label extends to taxonomic, not thematic associates. 'Dog' → other dogs, not bones. Substrate analogue: substrate's class-extension default.

concepts.name: child_directed_speech
concepts.definition: Motherese, parentese. Higher pitch, exaggerated intonation, simplified syntax, repetition. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-conditioning for learner.

concepts.name: joint_attention_acquisition
concepts.definition: Shared focus between caregiver + child. Foundation for word-learning. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared-context establishment.

concepts.name: negative_evidence_problem
concepts.definition: Children rarely receive explicit correction. Yet they don't permanently over-generalize. Substrate analogue: substrate's implicit-feedback learning.

concepts.name: second_language_acquisition
concepts.definition: L2 acquisition. Adults rarely reach native-like proficiency. Interference from L1. Substrate analogue: substrate's late-installed Mt incorporation.

concepts.name: fossilization
concepts.definition: L2 errors that persist despite continued exposure. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen-state pattern resistant to updating.

concepts.name: sign_language_acquisition
concepts.definition: Deaf children acquire signed languages with same milestones + universal features as spoken. Confirms language modality-independent. Substrate analogue: substrate's modality-flexible language faculty.

concepts.name: bilingual_acquisition
concepts.definition: Simultaneous acquisition of two languages from birth. Separate systems with some cross-talk. Native in both. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-Mt parallel acquisition.

rules.name: critical_period_constrains_native_acquisition
rules.head: the substrate begins language acquisition
rules.body: if past critical period (~puberty for humans), native-like competence is no longer achievable. Substrate's plasticity_override window.

rules.name: vocabulary_explosion_is_phase_transition
rules.head: the substrate accumulates words to a critical mass
rules.body: acquisition rate jumps discontinuously. Vocabulary explosion. Substrate's developmental phase transition pattern.

rules.name: statistical_learning_extracts_distributional_patterns
rules.head: the substrate hears sufficient input over time
rules.body: it tracks transitional probabilities + extracts patterns without explicit instruction. Saffran 1996. Substrate's distributional learning.

rules.name: child_constraints_solve_indeterminacy
rules.head: the substrate must associate a new word with a referent
rules.body: constraints (mutual exclusivity, whole object, taxonomic) narrow the hypothesis space. Markman. Substrate's biased Concept-formation.

rules.name: overregularization_indicates_rule_extraction
rules.head: the substrate produces 'goed' for past of 'go'
rules.body: it has extracted the regular rule + is over-applying. Sign of generalization, not regression. Substrate's rule-extraction phase.
